div.p: In the context of real-time fault-tolerant scheduling in Distributed Control systems, Primary-backup scheme plays an important role. A backup copy is always preferred to be executed as passive backup-copy whenever possible because it can take the advantages of backup copy de-allocation technique and overloading technique to improve schedulabilty. In this paper, we propose a novel Fault-tolerant Rate-Monotonic Best-fit algorithm (NRMBF) based on Distributed Control systems to enhance the schedulability. Unlike existing scheduling algorithms (FTRMBF or FTRMFF) that will allocate a new processor for backup copy when no existing processors can accommodate the current backup copy to be assigned. NRMBF uses a back tracing strategy that reassign the primary copy when the aforementioned situation occurs. As a result, NRMBF can use fewer processors to schedule a set of tasks without losing real-time and fault-tolerant capability of the system. Simulation results reveal that NRMBF significantly improves the schedulabilty over existing, comparable algorithms in literature.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Distributed Control Systems are increasingly being used for real-time applications because of their capability for high performance, reliability and extensibility. Due to the critical nature of tasks in a real-time system, it is essential that every task admitted in the system complete its execution even in the presence of faults [1]. As such, fault-tolerance is an inherent requirement for such systems.

Several approaches have been developed to achieve faulttolerance. From a hardware point of view, multiple replicas of essential application can be run on different hardware components to achieve fault-tolerance [2]. From a software point of view, it can be achieved by N-version programming or recovery blocks [3]. In addition, hybrid approaches of hardware and software can also be employed to achieve fault-tolerance [4]. However, a more efficient and effective way is through scheduling. On of the approaches used for fault-tolerant scheduling of real-time tasks is Primary-backup scheme. In this scheme, two versions of one task are scheduled on two different proces-sors and an acceptance test is used to check the correctness of the results [5,6,7]. The three variants of this scheme are: active backup-copy [5], passive backup-copy [6,12] ,and primarybackup copy overlapping [7].

In active backup-copy approach, the primary and backup copies of one task are executed concurrently [5]. It presents the advantages of requiring no synchronization between two copies-backup-copy can run before, after or concurrently with its primary copy-and imposing no constrains on execution time of tasks. However, the processor consumption time of a task in this approach is always twice of the task's processor consumption time. By contrast, a passive backup-copy is executed only if its corresponding primary copy fails to pass the acceptance test [6,12], otherwise it (backup-copy) can be deallocated from the schedule (this is the so-called backup copy de-allocation technique). Most importantly, the passive backup-copy presents the great advantage of backup copy overloading technique, that is many passive backup-copies whose primary copies have assigned to different processors can be scheduled on the same process so as to share the same time interval under the assumption of a single processor failure. Correspondingly, the passive backup-copy has the disadvantages of having tighter timing constraints. Primary backup-copy overlapping technique is a flexible approach wherein the primary copy and backup copy are scheduled to overlap in execution time [7].

Both active backup-copy and passive backup-copy are incorporated into the well-known Rate-Monotonic First-Fit assignment algorithm (FTRMFF) to achieve fault-tolerance [8]. FTRMFF takes a first-fit strategy to assign tasks to processors, that is assigning task copy (active or passive) to the first processor that could be fitted in. The intuition behind this strategy is that we should always try to use the existing processors to scheduling tasks. Yang C H proposed a best-fit algorithm based on a real-time fault-tolerant rate-monotonic algorithm, FTRMBF, which search all the existing processors trying to make as many backup copy to be executed as passive copy as possible to enhance system schedulability [9]. Yang F.M et. al proposed two techniques, namely task copies reallocation strategy and processors pre-allocation strategy, to enhance system schedulability [13]. Although all above scheduling algorithms can improve the system schedulability over FTRMFF to some extends, they will allocate a new processor for backup copy when no existing processors can accommodate the current backup copy to be assigned.

In the study, we propose a novel Fault-tolerant Rate-Monotonic Best-fit algorithm (NRMBF) based on Distributed Control Systems to enhance the schedulability. Unlike existing scheduling algorithms (FTRMBF or FTRMFF) that will allocate a new processor for backup copy when no existing processors can accommodate the current backup copy to be assigned. NRMBF uses a backup tracing strategy that reassign the primary copy when the aforementioned situation occurs. As a result, NRMBF can use fewer processors to schedule a set of tasks without losing real-time and fault-tolerant capability of the system.

The paper is organized as follow: In section 1, System model and assumption are presented. Section 2 proposes our strategy and scheduling algorithm. Simulation experiments and performance analysis are presented in section 3. Finally, section 4 concludes the paper by summarizing the main contribution of this paper and commenting on future directions of this work.

div.p: This section gives a formal definition of system model and presents our scheduling problem. Moreover, relevant assumptions are proposed.

div.head: A. Schedulability Algorithms Description
div.p: NRMBF goes in a way similar as RMBF and RMBF, the only difference between NRMBF and RMBF is that NRMBF will reassign the primary copy to a new processor when the current processors can not accommodate the backup copy.

Before task copies are assigned, both primary copy and backup copy are ordered by increasing period [8], namely, the priority of a copy is equal to the inverse of its period. It is worth noting that assigning task copies following decreasing RM priority could greatly simplify our algorithms. This is due to the fact that, when a task copy i is assigned to a processor, only lower priority task copy will be assigned to the same processor later. So the time intervals of i 's execution will remain unchanged after being assigned, and so does the WCRT of i . What's more, this will be very convenient to determine the status of backup-copy because the WCRT of primary copy will be unchanged [8].

The metric in our experiments is the number of processors required to assign a set of tasks. In the out come of the experiments, we denote with N the number processor used by NRMBF and M the number of processor required by FTRMBF. The outcome of the experiments is given in Fig. 4, which shows that both M and N increase proportionally with L. This is because as L increases, more processors are needed to schedule the set of tasks. Most importantly, it is clear that NRMBF ca n significantly save processors with respect to FTRMBF.

More over, Fig. 2 shows the values of (N-M)/M for the same experiments, which give the ratio of saving processors introduced by NRMBF with respect to FTRMBF. It is observed that when =0.5. The advantage of NRMBF over FTRMBF is mostly pronounced. This due to the fact that when =0.5 most backup-copy have the potential to be executed as passive backup-copy. The NRMBF has more ability to exploit such potential compared with FTRMBF. In summary, the NRMBF can saves 18.2%, 9.1% and 3.7% respect to FTRMBF for =0.5,0.2, and 08 respectively. The present paper analyzes the drawbacks of traditional First-Fit and Best-Fit algorithm, and propose a novel Faulttolerant Rate-Monotonic Best-fit algorithm (NRMBF) based on Distributed Control systems to enhance the schedulability Unlike existing scheduling algorithms (FTRMBF or FTRMFF) that will allocate a new processor for backup copy when no existing processors can accommodate the current backup copy to be assigned. NRMBF uses a back tracing strategy that reassign the primary copy when the aforementioned situation occurs. As a result, NRMBF can use fewer processors to schedule a set of tasks without losing real-time and fault-tolerant capability of the system. Experiments results show that NRMBF significantly out perform existing comparable algorithms in terms of schedulabilty, measured as number of processor needed to schedule a set of primary copies and its corresponding backup copies.
